# Map editor (`src/editor/`)

The creator edits the world map here: draws terrain and places objects (markers) at any zoom scale. Anything the creator does not draw is generated by the engine. See [engine instructions](./engine.instructions.md) for the quad tree, node states, lazy detail, persistence and determinism rules. They apply to everything here.

## Structure

- `canvas/CanvasRenderer.ts` renders the map. Drawing is split into commands in `canvas/commands/` (`drawTerrain`, `drawObjects`, `drawMarkers`, `drawGrid`, ...). `CanvasMatrix.ts` handles the view transform and `OverlayRenderer.ts` the overlay.
- `event-handlers/` handles input (draw, line, marker, move, select, zoom).
- `map/` holds the map React components, including the zoom level indicator.
- `sidebar/` and `topbar/` hold the tools UI.
- State lives in `src/store/editorStore.ts`.

## Rules when changing the editor

- Rendering reads from the quad tree. It must not assume a node's children exist. Zooming in triggers generation of the next detail level.
- Do not persist generated (`hydrated`/`empty`) data. Only detached, creator-drawn nodes are saved.
- Editing a generated node detaches it and locks its parents. Go through the engine's API for this instead of mutating tiles directly.
- Never put randomness in rendering or generation (see determinism rules). Visual variation must derive from seeds.
- Keep rendering cheap: draw only what is visible at the current scale and viewport.
